attempts.prompt: Soft editorial illustration of three pairs of women's eyes arranged side by side on a warm neutral background: one gently upturned, one level, one gently downturned, each with natural lashes and simple brows. Clean, modern beauty-magazine style with no text, labels or measurement lines.
issues: The three eyes do not clearly illustrate distinct canthal tilt categories. The left eye shows only a slight upward tilt, the middle eye is nearly level with a very faint upward angle, and the right eye is only marginally downturned. The differences are too subtle to convey positive, neutral and negative tilt at a glance, so the article's purpose is not met.

The eyes are not arranged as the brief specifies (upturned, level, downturned). They look like near-identical copies, with the first eye mainly distinguished by a winged liner, which adds a makeup variable that confuses the comparison.

The right eye appears to have a heavier upper lid or partial hooding, so the lid shape differs from the other two. This conflates lid shape with tilt and could mislead readers about what canthal tilt is.
The eyes are shown as floating isolated crops with soft vignetted skin edges. This looks slightly unnatural and offers no facial context or reference axis to help readers perceive tilt.
